blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Post-independence India faced three immediate challenges: accommodating diversity to shape a united nation, establishing democratic practices, and ensuring equitable economic development.
The integration of over 565 princely states into the Indian Union was led decisively by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel through the Instrument of Accession.
Partition led to tragic communal violence, mass displacement, and major refugee rehabilitation crises.
The States Reorganisation Act of 1956 reshaped state boundaries along linguistic lines following the Fazl Ali Commission recommendations.
Frequently tested: Integration cases of Hyderabad (Operation Polo), Junagadh (Plebiscite), and Jammu & Kashmir (Instrument of Accession).
Dhar Commission (1948), JVP Committee (1948), and Fazl Ali Commission (1953) regarding linguistic reorganisation of states.
Potti Sreeramulu's 56-day hunger strike leading to the creation of Andhra State in December 1952.
